newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM aims to end fresh government crisis.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM aims to end fresh government crisis.

text.p: The prime minister of the Baltic state of Latvia admitted on Friday that his squabbling, multi-party government was in crisis again and he would present a plan to bring order to his tottering administration.
"In reality, we are going through a government crisis," Prime Minister Andris Shkele told a news conference.
"Next week, I will present a plan to the political parties on how to get out of this situation," he added.
Shkele, a tough former businessman credited with injecting urgency into the former Soviet state's reforms, leads an unwieldy government of seven parties.
Due to party squabbles and corruption scandals, the government has lurched from crisis to crisis.
Fresh problems erupted as two ministers were forced to quit in a corruption row after they combined state and private jobs.

A third minister's future is in doubt amid similar allegations, while Interior Minister Dainis Turlais handed in his resignation after eight children were killed at a firefighting show when the basket they were in fell from a crane.
Shkele refused to give details on the measures that he would propose to end the fresh crisis.
Shkele has resigned once already, when President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject his candidate for finance minister. He was reappointed after solving his differences with the president.
Despite the political infighting, Shkele has managed to pursue the reforms and financial discipline that have brought a balanced budget, falling inflation and a faster pace of privatisation.
